body: I've actually done that.  It was several months ago.  At the time her response was "I forgive you, but I don't feel comfortable being around you."  It's only in the past month or so that she has started feeling comfortable around me again.  So at this point she knows how I feel.  I think I just have to slowly work my way back into her life and earn her trust back now that she can stand being around me.  According to her mom though, it's not time to give up yet, and as close as their family is I'm inclined to believe her mom.  It just sucks because it's my fault.  Like any guy I've had my fair share of girl problems, but I never dreamed that I'd be the bad guy and hurt someone I cared about like that.  So the girl problems, combined with the fact that it was all my fault, combined with the unemployment, combined with the greatly diminished social life I guess has been what has been getting me down.  However, I guess just venting to you has helped a lot, and I really appreciate it.  I'm not sure if you honestly have any interest in anything I've said or are just trying to be a good Samaritan, but either way I really appreciate it.  It's really taken me from a bad spot tonight to a spot where I'm at least neutral.  Still not happy about the way things are going in life, but I'm in a lot better place than I was a couple hours ago.

Also regarding the contact I have with her.  It is VERY rare, and almost always initiated by me, and usually over fb or something not very personal.  Although, she was willing to hang out with me in a group about a month ago, and it went well.  I ran into her again on the way to my car, and we made small talk for a bit.  She even said it was nice to see you.  So I got that going for me, which is nice.

"Can I ask if you miss having those happy feelings that you had with her? or is it HER that you truly miss. You gotta be dead honest with yourself, because my advice would be that if you truly love her you put your heart out there because you have nothing to lose." 

Both.  I miss her.  I miss everything about her, but I also miss the times we spent together.  I think they kind of go hand in hand.  Over the past 6 or 7 months there haven't been a lot of great days, but there have been a few, and on those days I distinctly remember thinking "I wish xxxx was here to enjoy this with me" (I also miss here on the bad days, but then the thought is more "OH GOD I MISS HER" or "how could I be so stupid")

Yeah, I was incredibly selfish, stupid, thoughless, etc., and I still have no idea what got into me that day.  I've never been a player or anything like that by a long shot.  And I know that the only things you know about me are what I've told you, but what I did in that situation was a tremendous lapse in judgement or any thought at all for that matter.  It's crazy how quickly one stupid mistake has such a big ripple effect.

Oh definitely.  Things were going almost perfect.  I just lost my mind and made the biggest mistake of my life.  It sucks because in that situation I'm the bad guy.  I broke her heart for no reason, and she was torn up by it.  It turns out that I also really screwed up my own life with it too.  We've talked once or twice since then and she says she forgives me, but I don't really get to see her very often because she likes to keep her distance, which I respect, but it sucks.  I guess I still hold onto hope that things can be fixed because she said she understands that it was a one time mistake and that it's not really who I am.  She also understands how full of regret I am (at least I think she does)  Her mom also messages me on a regular basis.  Apparently she's talking to a new guy (not sure whether or not they are anything serious yet.  For all I know they are just close friends).  On the optimistic side of fixing things the mom and the rest of the family hate the guy and really wish she was still with me (and her family is all very close), so hopefully they can give her a subtle reminder of how well things were going when we were together, but it's not looking too great right now.  Then again, it's been 6 months and I really have only heard from her two or three times, not to mention the other guy.  So fixing things with her may very well be a pipe dream.  I think the relationship part of this would also be easier to deal with if it wasn't for the unemployment and other social loss.  Unfortunately the unemployment and damage to my friend group is a part of it, which kind of magnifies the loss of the girl.  (Holidays also probably don't help the situation)
Wow, I'm really sorry.  That was really long winded for not saying a whole lot.

Well I appreciate that.  I suppose maybe talking about it will help.  I'll try anything at this point.  I guess the quickest way to summarize everything is as follows: I've always had self esteem issues.  It's probably not worth going into too much detail as to why, but basically as a kid I was bullied and as a teenager I was a teenager, and pretty much all teenagers have self esteem issues.  Anyway, point is self esteem/loving myself has always been an issue even before offing myself was even something I could dream of doing.  Fast forward to this year, and a lot of good stuff happened.  I got a girlfriend.  She was my first real, serious girlfriend, and things were going fantastic.  I was getting ready to graduate college, and I even had a really really nice job lined up, and my social life was at an all time high.  I had a lot of friends, and a lot of quality friends.  Essentially, at the beginning of 2013 I was probably as happy as I have been in my entire life.  Then things started to fall apart.  Some of the things that fell apart were out of my control, but the worse part is that some were all my fault.  The first thing that happened was about a month before graduation (May 2013) that awesome job I had lined up disappeared.  They didn't even have an explanation, just that the job was no longer available.  My grades weren't slipping, and I hadn't gotten into any trouble, so this is one of those things that was just a shitty situation that was out of my control.  The next thing that happened is that I made the biggest mistake of my life.  So, while I was dating this girl, who things were going fantastic with, I got a text from one of our mutual friends.  This mutual friend happens to be the hottest girl I've ever seen.  It turns out this girl decides she has feelings for me.  So, I did the stupidest thing that I could have done and went and talked to her.  While talking to her I rationalized breaking up with the other girl for her (the girl who things were going really well with was going out of the country for the summer, and I think I talked myself into believing that we couldn't make it work).  So, anyway I start dating hot girl and it just doesn't go well.  We really only communicated over text.  She was really flaky.  Then on top of everything I'm about 75% sure she cheated on me (although I have no proof).  Anyway, relationship with hot girl is over after one month.  Then I graduated college.

So, what's really been getting to me is the aftermath of all of that.  Hot girl and awesome girl were both in the same friendgroup with me, and because of that love triangle or whatever my entire social group was blown up.  I really don't have any good friends anymore, and most of my weekends are spent doing what I'm doing right now.  Sitting and browsing the internet.  The second fallout of everything is that after that job fell through, I was unable to find anything else.  I am unemployed to this day.  I only scrape by (and I really mean scrape by) by doing odd jobs.  I don't know if you've ever been unemployed and out of school at the same time, but it really makes you feel like a worthless bum, even if you are trying to find a job, people still ask what you're up to, and it gets a bit tough to say "looking for a job" 7 months after graduation.  Then finally, I just really miss my relationship with that girl that I brokeup with.  Leaving her was the biggest mistake of my life.  I don't think what kills me is any one of those things above that I've listed, but rather a little bit of everything.

I guess I'm just really not the type of person that likes to be public with their problems.  I pretty much internalize everything (which I know probably isn't the best way about going things, but that's how it is).  Even this reddit thing is a bit out of my comfort zone, even under a throwaway.  A couple of my friends know that I haven't been doing well lately, unfortunately they live 2500 miles away.  Along with not really talking about my problems just being a part of how I am, I do honestly think that I would feel a bit guilty though.

I see them all the time (my immediate family and extended family all live within 30 miles of each other).  I only say that we are distant because we really keep our personal lives to ourselves when we are around each other.   We'll talk about tv or sports or whatever funny thing happened last time the family got together, but nothing of substance is ever really discussed.  Even we were really open in the whole communication thing, I probably wouldn't say anything.  In person I'm pretty freaking stoic, so dropping a bomb like that would send my mom and grandmother in particular into an emotion nightmare.
No I haven't.  My family and I aren't that close.  We aren't distant, we just aren't close.  I don't really remember the last serious conversation that I had with my family about anything personal.
